WITH deduplicated_weather AS (
    -- Remove duplicates by keeping the first record for each location_id + date
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (location_id, date)
        location_id,
        date,
        max_temp_c,
        min_temp_c,
        avg_temp_c
    FROM daily_weather
    WHERE 
        -- Filter out records where all temperature values are NULL
        (max_temp_c IS NOT NULL OR min_temp_c IS NOT NULL OR avg_temp_c IS NOT NULL)
        -- Filter out unreasonable temperature values (basic data quality check)
        AND (max_temp_c IS NULL OR (max_temp_c >= -100 AND max_temp_c <= 60))
        AND (min_temp_c IS NULL OR (min_temp_c >= -100 AND min_temp_c <= 60))
        AND (avg_temp_c IS NULL OR (avg_temp_c >= -100 AND avg_temp_c <= 60))
    ORDER BY location_id, date, max_temp_c DESC NULLS LAST
),
monthly_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        location_id,
        TO_CHAR(date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
        ROUND(AVG(avg_temp_c)::numeric, 1) AS monthly_avg_temp,
        ROUND(MIN(min_temp_c)::numeric, 1) AS monthly_min_temp,
        ROUND(MAX(max_temp_c)::numeric, 1) AS monthly_max_temp,
        COUNT(*) AS days_with_data
    FROM deduplicated_weather
    WHERE 
        -- Ensure we have at least one valid temperature reading
        avg_temp_c IS NOT NULL OR min_temp_c IS NOT NULL OR max_temp_c IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY location_id, TO_CHAR(date, 'YYYY-MM')
)
SELECT
    l.name AS location_name,
    l.country,
    ma.month,
    ma.monthly_avg_temp,
    ma.monthly_min_temp,
    ma.monthly_max_temp,
    ma.days_with_data
FROM monthly_aggregates ma
JOIN locations l ON ma.location_id = l.location_id
ORDER BY l.name, ma.month;
